From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

John — thanks for the recap and great questions. Summary + recommended next steps below.

Recap (1-line): RAG for multi-doc customer support; priority = high-quality grounding (low hallucination) with <200ms added query latency target for conversational UI.

Recommended model variants (short rationale):
- Llama 2 70B Chat (quantized) — Best quality for complex, multi-hop answers; higher token cost and latency. Good if grounding precision is top priority.
- Mistral Medium / Redwood-13B Chat (8-bit) — Strong quality/latency balance; lower cost and often sufficient for short support answers.
- Falcon-40B Instruct (optimized) — Good mid-point; faster on CPU/GPU combos and easier to run in dedicated/private deployments.

RAG / retrieval + reranker recommendations (summary):
- Retriever: hybrid (bm25 initial filter -> vector ANN HNSW) with top_k=100, neural reranking down to top_n=8.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (smaller cross-encoder fine-tuned on your support corpus) for best grounding precision. If latency is very tight, use a bi-encoder + calibrated scores as fallback.

Evals & metrics we provide (attached + links):
- Precision@1 (grounded answers matching doc source), MRR@5, Recall@100, Hallucination Rate (manual eval sampling), Answer Factuality (human-rated).
- Attached: acme_rag_eval_summary.pdf (high-level results from our pilot with your 10k doc sample), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (example prompts we ran), acme_corpus_sample_10k.jsonl (sample doc set).
- Benchmark link: https://docs.redwood.com/rag-benchmarks#acme

Quality regression concerns and guardrails:
- We'll baseline on your prompt_set_v1. If model updates cause >3% drop in Precision@1 or >5% increase in Hallucination Rate on the test prompts, we trigger a rollback and quality incident.
- Recommend adding a small human-in-the-loop evaluation for first 2 weeks of production.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We run an extended eval with your full 100k doc export (estimate 3–5 days compute) using the three model variants above.
2) Priyom will scope retrieval + reranker finetune options and estimate delta in precision/latency.
3) Schedule technical working session next week to align on metrics, sample prompts, and timeline.

I attached the summary + prompt set. Let me know availability for a 60-min technical session next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME RAG discovery — retrieval & reranker notes

Quick technical notes from the infra/ML side (putting numbers to Marissa's summary):

- Retrieval pipeline:
  * Stage 1 (token/keyword candidate): BM25 with standard English analyzer, return top_k=300 to ensure recall on short KB entries.
  * Stage 2 (vector ANN): use FAISS HNSW (index_dim=1536, ef_search=128) on embeddings (sentence-transformers / 1536-d). Return top_k=100.
  * Stage 3 (rerank): cross-encoder re-ranker (roberta-large-cross-encoder style) fine-tuned on your support Q/A pairs — rerank top_100 -> top_n=8.

- Latency / throughput tradeoffs:
  * Cross-encoder reranker adds ~40–90ms per query depending on instance (GPU recommended). If we need <100ms tail latency, we can: reduce top_k/ef_search or use a distilled cross-encoder.

- Evaluation metrics to capture:
  * grounding_precision@1 (automated + sampled human verification), MRR@5, Recall@100, hallucination_rate (human labeling), average_tokens_per_response, median_latency_p95.

- Reranker choices:
  * Default: cross-encoder for production grounding-critical flows.
  * Fallback: bi-encoder + calibrated confidence threshold for low-latency interactive flows.

I'll prepare a short runbook and cost estimate for the three model variants and share later today.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
